UTC’s acquisition of the Doctors Building in 2000 marked an important moment in the growth of campus. Located at the southwest corner of McCallie Avenue and Palmetto Street, the real estate purchase marked the University’s first expansion south across McCallie Avenue.
 Planned in 1955 by Atlanta-based realtor Sam Massell Jr., the structure was originally a professional office building for physicians, surgeons, dentists and other healthcare providers. Interior spaces were outfitted with laboratory gas lines, exhaust fans, heavy-duty X-ray wiring and configured for the “Music by Muzak” system.
 🔗  Learn more here: https://blog.utc.edu/…/if-these-walls-could-talk-doctors-b…/

Heads up, Collegedale!
 On October 7, 8, and 10, you may notice a couple of small cameras along the Wolftever Greenway, near Veterans Memorial Park. No need for concern — these are temporary pedestrian and bicycle counters, not surveillance devices.

 Why it matters: This data helps the City pursue grant funding to extend and enhance our greenway trail system, supporting our efforts to expand walkability and alternative travel options throughout Collegedale.
 We appreciate our residents helping make Collegedale an even more connected, walkable community! 
 Questions or concerns about the count period or device placement? Contact us at (423) 396-3135.

 Hamilton County, TN – On the morning of September 30, 2026, Tyner Middle High Academy school administration searched a student’s vehicle after a parent expressed their concerns about a potential firearm on campus.
 A loaded AR-15 was found inside the vehicle, and HCSO school resource deputies seized the firearm and took the 17-year-old juvenile suspect into custody.
 The juvenile faces the following charge:
 • Possession of a Firearm on School Property
 This information is preliminary and subject to change. No further details are available.
 Disclaimer: The HCSO does not release identifying information regarding juvenile suspects.

items.title: Every Friday afternoon, a vibrant and talented group of ladies known affectionately as the Hixson Hookers convenes to cr...
items.content_text:
Every Friday afternoon, a vibrant and talented group of ladies known affectionately as the Hixson Hookers convenes to crochet, knit, and socialize. While you might occasionally catch them crafting custom jewelry or exploring other creative ideas, their true passion lies in the rhythm of knitting and crocheting. 
 The group recently poured their hearts into a heartwarming community project. Together, they hand-crafted and donated approximately fifteen beautiful lap blankets for the residents of a local memory and behavioral facility in Hixson. 
 The delivery was an absolute joy. The residents picked out a blanket of their exact choosing. They were truly excited to receive their colorful and cozy new items! This is exactly the kind of meaningful, community-driven activity we want to sustain. Hixson Hooker's plan to continue this heartwarming tradition for years to come proved that a little yarn, a lot of laughter, and a bit of teamwork can make a massive difference. 
 Join Our Hooked on Crochet Class every Friday at Hixson Community Center | 2:30-3:30 PM

This Saturday, October 3rd, marks 100 years of tradition, community, and great golf right here in Chattanooga! Since opening its doors on October 3, 1926, Brainerd Golf Course has been a beloved home for everyday golfers.   Here are a few fast facts as we look back on 100 incredible years:
 The course was designed by legendary Scottish golf architect Donald Ross—the genius behind world-famous courses like Pinehurst No. 2! 
 Opening Day Flashback: When Brainerd opened on October 3, 1926, green fees were just $0.50!   
 The original clubhouse was designed by local architect Clarence Jones, who went on to design Chattanooga's landmark Jones Observatory and National Guard Armory.  
 A huge thank you to all the players, staff, and community members who have made Brainerd Golf Course a staple of Chattanooga sports and public recreation for a century.

items.title: Cuts in official development assistance (ODA) for health are concentrated in countries that rely most on external financ...
items.content_text:
Cuts in official development assistance (ODA) for health are concentrated in countries that rely most on external financing.
 ODA is financial support from governments promoting the economic development and welfare of developing countries.
 #OECD projections show that bilateral ODA for health could fall to its lowest level in almost two decades.
 Some of the steepest reductions are expected in sub-Saharan Africa, where many countries rely on aid to support their health systems.
 ➡️ Uganda could see bilateral health ODA fall by 53.5% between 2024 and 2026.
 ➡️ Malawi and South Sudan could see declines of 50.8% and 42.4% respectively. External financing accounts for around 60% of current health expenditure in both countries.
 ➡️ Other recipient countries, including Mozambique and Lesotho, where external finance matters, are also projected to face significant reductions.
 Health is projected to experience the deepest cuts of any ODA sector between 2024 and 2026.
 For countries with limited fiscal space to replace declining support, these reductions could place additional pressure on already constrained health systems.
 Explore the latest data on ODA for health ➡️ https://brnw.ch/21x64mA

Help us welcome Bryan Massey to Chattanooga Comic Con! Join Bryan and other amazing talent at the Chattanooga Convention Center, November 7th-8th!
 Bryan Massey has built a prolific career in voice acting since earning his breakout role as the violent Chicago gangster Ladd Russo in Baccano!, a performance that won him a Dubby Award in 2009 and established his distinctive gravelly voice as a signature in the industry. Born in Michigan and raised in Dallas, Massey combined his unique vocal instrument with a natural sense of humor to carve out a niche in anime dubbing, video games, and on-screen work that has spanned hundreds of recognizable characters across multiple decades.
 His extensive anime credits include Cocytus in Overlord, Monkey D. Dragon in One Piece, Oolong throughout the Dragon Ball franchise, Dick Gumshoe in Ace Attorney, Tenshiro Okakura in Rideback, and Teppei Hōjō in Higurashi: When They Cry.
 Beyond animation, Massey has appeared in major feature films including Detective Brinkley in Mad Money with Diane Keaton and Ted Danson, Skeeter in Oliver Stone’s W, and Officer Lerma in the Nicolas Cage thriller Drive Angry.
 His video game work includes Wilhelm in Borderlands: The Pre-Sequel and multiple roles in the Dragon Ball Xenoverse series. Whether lending his voice to heroes, villains, or memorable supporting characters, Massey brings authenticity and energy to every performance.

items.content_text:
Chattanooga firefighters are credited with stopping a house fire from spreading Tuesday night. At 9:31 PM, Red Shift companies were dispatched to a reported residential structure fire in the 4900 Bal Harbor Circle. 
 Engine 6 arrived on scene and Captain Chad McBryar established command of a large, two-story home with heavy fire and smoke showing from the side and back of the structure. Engine 6, Ladder 6, and Engine 4 made an aggressive interior attack, finding heavy fire and smoke on the interior and exterior, as well as in the attic space over the garage. Squad 7 and Ladder 7 arrived on scene and assisted with fire suppression efforts. All occupants had evacuated the residence prior to CFDs arrival. The fire was extinguished in approximately 20 minutes with no injuries. The cause is under investigation.
 Engine 6, Ladder 6, Ladder 7, Squad 7, Engine 4, Battalion 2, Battalion 3, and CFD Investigations responded.

Athens Area Council for the Arts (AACA) is seeking an executive director to lead this vibrant organization as it builds upon its mission to enrich the quality of life in the community by providing opportunities for the expression and appreciation of the arts. The deadline for applications is September 30, 2026. 
 Reporting to a Board of Directors, the Executive Director is responsible for providing leadership and strategic direction in all aspects of organizational management. 
 The position requires a dynamic leader with a passion for the arts and the ability to build relationships with diverse stakeholders. 
 Since its founding in 1979, AACA + The Arts Center has grown to support a wide variety of opportunities in the performing and visual arts. 
 “Our commitment to quality and dedication to delivering exciting ways to experience the arts has helped us grow into an arts and cultural hub for our region,” said Mike Dannel, AACA Board of Directors President. 
 To accommodate its growing programming, The Arts Center recently acquired and renovated three buildings to provide much-needed space for new classes and performances.
 More information about the position and how to apply for this opportunity is available at athensartscouncil.org/hiring-executive-director. Please apply by September 30.

 Saturday, October 3
 4:00 PM–5:00 PM
 Downtown Library Auditorium, 1st Floor

 Echoes of Chattanooga draws from historic oral histories held in the Chattanooga Public Library’s Local History and Genealogy Department, telling the stories of twelve Chattanoogans through Peggy’s original poetic monologues.  The event will include the premiere staged reading of Peggy’s monologues and the launch of the illustrated companion book, featuring artwork by Russell Robinson and published by Walnut Street Publishing .
 Join us Saturday to hear Peggy talk about the people, stories, and history behind Echoes of Chattanooga.

items.title: Performance Space Alliance Opens New Community Rehearsal Space After more than a year of research, conversations, planni...
items.content_text:
Performance Space Alliance Opens New Community Rehearsal Space
 After more than a year of research, conversations, planning, and collaboration, Chattanooga’s performing arts feasibility study is moving from ideas into action. With support from ArtsBuild and the Lyndhurst Foundation, the process identified one of the most pressing challenges facing local performing artists and organizations: a serious lack of consistent, accessible rehearsal space. More than 100 interviews, multiple phases of study, and the work of a Governance Committee of local arts leaders have now led to the launch of a pilot shared-space program. Located in the North Shore/Hixson area, the new facility includes two large group spaces, three rehearsal rooms, a green room, conference room, shared office space, and a small traditional stage. More than a dozen groups are participating, with over 150 performers expected to use the space in its first week alone.
 The project is also entering this exciting new chapter with a new name: the Performance Innovation Center is now the Performance Space Alliance (PSA), reflecting its mission to bring the creative community together around affordable, shared spaces. Rehearsal space is only the beginning, with future goals including performance, shop, and storage space. The community can help this effort grow by donating needed equipment and furnishings, including mirrors, speakers, a marley dance floor, and ballet barres, or by making a financial contribution. Those interested in supporting the project, learning more, or inquiring about rehearsal, classroom, or office space can contact Blake Harris at blake@artsbuild.com.

items.content_text:
Dear former Highland Park Baptist Church/ Tennessee Temple University members/ leaders and students! 
 I am Kevin Wallace, Pastor of the Redemption To The Nations Church, which is located in the property  that was formally the Highland Park Baptist Church.
 We are in the process of planning and preparing for a series of projects in the future, that will renovate some old buildings on the property and build new ones where an arson destroyed the two historic buildings several years ago. 
 The expansion is obviously about the future generations and families that are a part of the Redemption To The Nations Church family. But I can't help but think about the rich history and all of the souls saved and ministries  launched from that campus over the years. While some have chosen to focus on the differences between Highland Park Baptist and Redemption To The Nations Church, I have maintained gratitude and thanksgiving to God for the rich history that the property has and I've done my best to honor the ministry of Dr. Roberson and The HPBC for the 13 years we have been there.

Commission Workshop Recap – Sept. 28
 Workshops let the Commission dig into items before a formal vote. No votes were taken, but here's what was discussed:
 Christmas Parade
 Based on 583 survey responses, the parade is planned for Sunday, Dec. 13 at 3:00 PM. Respondents preferred a Sunday (66%) afternoon (69%) parade, and 51% wanted it held separately from the tree lighting. Staff is finalizing route details & the commission appreciates the input from the community.
 Iron Rail Cams
 A proposal would place a railroad camera at Thatcher Switch Recreation Area, with equipment, installation, and maintenance provided at no cost to the city. The camera can pan and tilt to view trains in both directions, and the feed could be linked on the city's website. The Commission had no objections, and the item will return for a future vote. Commissioner Johnson would like to explore a train-watching seating area.
 Little Debbie Parkway ROW Abandonments
 Two abandonment requests from 2025 were reviewed. Of the roughly 2.6 acres requested in the first, the city owns only 0.598 acres. The rest belongs to the State and Hamilton County, so the applicant would need to go through them. The second request (about 0.23 acres near Jac Cate Road) is state-owned and would go through TDOT's Excess Land Office. Staff is asking the County and State to notify the city before making any moves so sidewalk and trail expansion can be discussed.
 Airport Funding
 The City Manager explained why the airport fund should keep a healthy reserve. The FY 26-27 airport budget projects a surplus of $78,670, and the fund holds about $1 million in reserves. Keeping four to six months of operating funds (roughly $500,000–$600,000) is good financial practice. A loan is possible for the retaining wall project should the commission favor that route, and staff will know more once numbers come back.
 Commissioner Reports
 Commissioner Johnson mentioned traffic delays on Ooltewah Ringgold Road from the gas pipeline project have been minimal. Vice Mayor Sadler floated the idea of a food pantry at the library, and staff will follow up.
 👉 Read the full recap: https://www.collegedaletn.gov/news_detail_T8_R429.php

items.content_text:
Countries across Latin America and the Caribbean have made major progress in expanding access to healthcare. But access alone does not guarantee better health outcomes.
 Avoidable deaths remain nearly twice as high as the #OECD average. For example, people living with cancer face persistent gaps in early diagnosis, treatment and continuity of care.
 At the same time, only 6 of 19 countries report comprehensive national systems for measuring quality, and paying providers based on quality remains uncommon.
 The next challenge is moving from coverage to care that is effective, safe and people-centred.
 Learn more about health systems across the region in the new #HealthAtAGlance: Latin America and the Caribbean 2026:
 https://brnw.ch/21x62FV

CPD Investigating Deadly Crash on I-24 WB
 CHATTANOOGA, Tenn. -- The Chattanooga Police Department (CPD) is investigating a deadly crash that occurred on I-24 WB Monday night.
 Shortly before 9:30 p.m., CPD's Traffic Unit responded to a multivehicle crash near the Rossville Boulevard exit on I-24 WB. Preliminary findings indicate a motorcyclist driving at a high rate of speed crashed into the back of a tractor-trailer.
 The motorcycle rider, a 22-year-old man, was pronounced dead at the scene.
 These findings are preliminary and subject to change as the investigation continues.
 #CPDnews

items.content_text:
The decisions made at the ballot box can show up in our everyday lives.
 Who makes decisions about your schools?
 Who has a say in healthcare?
 Who decides how public money is spent?
 Who makes the laws that affect your work, your housing, and your community?
 Those decisions are connected to the people and issues on your ballot.
 That’s why it’s not enough to know when to vote. We need to know what and who we’re voting on.
 Before you vote, take some time to learn:
 🗳️ Who’s on your ballot
 🗳️ What office they’re running for
 🗳️ What that office is responsible for
 🗳️ What the candidates have said and done
 🗳️ What each ballot measure would actually change
 The biggest race on your ballot isn’t the only one that matters. Local races and ballot measures can have a direct impact on your community, too.
